expected_evidence: Geological: a continent-spanning 'YD boundary layer' (~12.9 ka) showing platinum, iridium, and other siderophile-element spikes consistent with an extraterrestrial input, as claimed by proponents of the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis
Geological: nanodiamonds, magnetic microspherules, and carbon spherules/aciniform soot in lake, marine, and loess sediments dated to YD onset
Geological/astronomical: a 'black mat' organic-rich layer marking abrupt ecological transition at multiple North American and Eurasian sites

Astronomical: cosmic dust/micrometeorite flux anomaly in Greenland or Antarctic ice cores at ~12.9 ka; search for a corresponding impact crater or airburst structure (e.g., proposed Hiawatha Glacier crater, though independently dated later)
Geological: proxy evidence of an abrupt North Atlantic meltwater pulse (freshwater lens, salinity/oxygen-isotope shift, AMOC slowdown signatures) coincident with the cooling onset
Material/archaeological: continent-wide wildfire/biomass-burning charcoal spike and disruption or discontinuity in Clovis-era archaeological assemblages in North America
Genetic: megafauna population bottleneck or extinction signatures and human population bottleneck around 12.9 ka in ancient DNA records
Oral_tradition: flood, fire-from-sky, or catastrophe myths among circum-Atlantic/Native American groups (very low-confidence, speculative link)

Model-prior: prior published impact-hypothesis literature (Firestone et al. 2007 and follow-ups) proposing exactly this actor-mechanism-object chain, alongside numerous failed-replication studies attributing the same markers to non-impact causes (wildfire-produced nanodiamonds, terrestrial mineral misidentification)
response.rationale: This hypothesis conflates two distinct, actively-debated mechanisms for Younger Dryas onset: the mainstream meltwater-pulse/AMOC-shutdown model and the more speculative cosmic-airburst (Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis, YDIH) model, treating the airburst as the trigger for the meltwater pulse itself. Using the 'younger-dryas' period row (interval matches YD onset, ~12.9-11.7 ka, i.e. roughly -11000 to -10001 in this schema's convention) as the closest bucket: geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7) detectability are both comparatively high for this period because ice cores, varved lake sediments, and loess/paleosol boundary layers from this exact interval are well-preserved and have been intensively sampled by multiple independent labs worldwide. Material (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence are moderate — Clovis-era sites and megafaunal remains exist but are sparse and taphonomically patchy for Upper Paleolithic populations. Oral tradition (0.1) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially non-recoverable at this time depth. Textual evidence is impossible (0.0), pre-dating writing by ~8000 years. Given that geological/astronomical detectability is already fairly good, the fact that decades of targeted searches (platinum/iridium spikes, nanodiamonds, spherules, ice-core dust flux) have produced mixed, heavily contested, and largely non-replicated results is meaningful negative evidence — it is not simply an artifact of low detectability. This favors treating the cosmic-airburst-triggering-meltwater-pulse claim as scientifically weak/likely false rather than merely 'undetected,' while the underlying meltwater-pulse-caused-YD-cooling claim (without the airburst mechanism) remains geologically well-supported. I suggest a modest overall detectability_adjustment of 0.55 — slightly below the geological/astronomical ceiling of 0.65-0.7 to reflect that direct causal attribution (airburst → meltwater pulse → AMOC shutdown) is much harder to demonstrate than any single proxy layer, even though the proxies themselves are reasonably well preserved and searchable. All specific claims about published impact-marker studies (Firestone et al.) beyond what's given here are drawn from model-prior/training knowledge, not from evidence text explicitly provided in this task, and should be treated as unverified.
